newsitem.title: UK: ITF says tanker delays minimal in industrial action.
newsitem.headline: ITF says tanker delays minimal in industrial action.

text.p: Oil tankers will be among vessels targeted by an International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF) week of action starting on May 12, but delays to them are likely to be minimal, the union said.
The ITF has announced it will hold a week of industrial action across Europe against flag of convenience (FOC) ships from May 12 to May 16. It said seafarers and dockers would take part.

The term flag of convenience refers to ships flying the flag which is not the national flag of the country of the owner and the ITF has long said FOC registers tend to have more substandard ships and poorer wages than national registers.
"We will hit oil tankers if they do not have ITF-acceptable collective agreements," ITF spokesman Richard Flint said.
However, he said, "Strikes do not usually last more than one or two hours. We are aware of the safety ramifications of holding up tanker loadings."
He added, "We have agreements with a number of oil majors and even though a number of companies now charter in, we generally find that tankers are well maintained."
The FOC campaign is already active in Scandinavian countries and action may be concentrated on boycotts of southern European ports.
"We are active in some oil terminals, particularly in Italy, and we organise some chemical workers at oil facilities," he added.
The campaign will involve all 15 shipping registers classified as FOC by the ITF, but Flint said 60 percent of Liberian-flagged ships, one of the world's biggest registers, have ITF agreements.
"As long as those agreements are honoured, they will have no problem," he said.
